metadata.title: SFTC Cricket Level-Based Teaching Database
metadata.description: App-facing cricket teaching progressions by domain and level, derived from structured cricket research drafts.

sport_teaching_progressions.learning_goal: Build a repeatable setup and safe straight-bat scoring foundation before expanding shot range.
teaching_priorities: basic grip and bat face control
avoid_until_ready: heavy rotational gym work before movement control
progression_signals: can choose leave/defend/drive in simple feeds
coach_notes: Do not force one ideal stance; stabilize outcomes first.
Technique should support seeing the ball and controlling contact, not looking textbook.

sport_teaching_progressions.learning_goal: Add adaptable footwork, pace/spin decision-making, strike rotation, and role-specific scoring options.
suitable_for: users who can handle basic net pace
teaching_priorities: shot selection by line and length
technical_focus: bat path matched to shot family
avoid_until_ready: too many new shots in one block
advanced ramp/reverse options without base control
max power work during high batting load
progression_signals: can explain plan vs pace and spin
can keep shape under variable feeds
coach_notes: Intermediate batting should create choices, not just more shots.
Use scenario constraints so the batter learns why a shot is selected.

sport_teaching_progressions.learning_goal: Specialize batting plans by role, format, bowler type, field, conditions, and match state.
practice_design: scenario nets with field and score
avoid_until_ready: new high-risk shots in competition week
max effort power hitting with back/wrist pain
fatigue-only volume with no decision quality
progression_signals: has reliable scoring option against each bowling family
can state match role and risk budget
coach_notes: Advanced does not mean random innovation; it means better decisions under more constraints.
Power work should preserve contact quality.

coach_notes: Intermediate pace work is about controllable weapons, not novelty.

coach_notes: Beginner spin is control first.
Variation interest should not unlock advanced skills without stock-ball accuracy.
